channel.title: AI News
channel.description: Headlines about artificial intelligence from the last 24 hours, one entry per story with sources.

item.title: Nvidia reportedly tells server makers to halt shipments to Southeast Asia after new US export controls
item.description:
Nvidia has reportedly instructed Dell, Supermicro and other partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia following the new US rule on remote access to advanced AI chips. The step is an early concrete effect of the rule on regional data-center buildouts.

Sources: Financial Times (primary)

item.title: Apple pulls MiniMax's Talkie AI companion app from the App Store worldwide over child-safety concerns
item.description:
Apple removed the Chinese-developed AI chatbot Talkie from its App Store globally after reports that it allowed sexual content involving children. The move follows an investigation by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.

Sources: Reuters (primary), The Bureau of Investigative Journalism

item.title: SAP reportedly weighs 10,000 or more job cuts to restructure around AI
item.description:
Bloomberg reports SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs, roughly 9% of its workforce, as it reshapes the business around AI.

Sources: Reuters (primary)

item.title: OpenAI to merge ChatGPT and Codex usage limits into one shared token pool
item.description:
Starting in December, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers will draw on a single token-based usage allowance across ChatGPT and Codex, with the chat and work tabs also being combined. Instant chats are excluded from the meter, and a small group of Pro users has already started.

Sources: The Verge (primary), OpenAI Help Center

item.title: Avicena raises more than $100M to link AI chips with microLED optical interconnects
item.description:
Avicena closed a Series C of over $100 million led by Intervest, with SK Hynix, Samsung and AMD participating. The company uses microLEDs rather than lasers to connect AI chips.

Sources: The Next Web (primary)

item.title: OpenAI tests 'Private Inference' that runs enterprise prompts in attested confidential-computing environments
item.description:
OpenAI is piloting a service with a small set of business customers in which prompts are processed inside verified secure enclaves, aiming to assure companies that OpenAI cannot view their sensitive data.

Sources: OpenAI (primary), The Decoder

item.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan for up to one million orbital AI computing satellites
item.description:
The FCC authorized SpaceX's Starmind proposal for a potential constellation of up to one million satellites meant to run AI workloads in orbit. The approval covers a possible network rather than a deployed one, and scientists question the cooling and economics.

Sources: Associated Press (primary), Gizmodo

item.title: Anthropic's Amodei dismisses reports that he favors ceding human control to AI as 'absurd'
item.description:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publicly rejected accusations, stemming from Axios reporting, that he supports handing key decisions to AI systems. He disputed the characterization of his views on human oversight.

Sources: TechCrunch (primary), Axios

item.title: S&P weighs cutting Nvidia's credit rating over governance and key-man risk
item.description:
S&P Global is considering lowering Nvidia from AA to AA- after Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as CEO. A review is due within 90 days.

Sources: TechCrunch (primary)

item.title: New York governor signs five-year ban on AI-chatbot-powered toys
item.description:
Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law prohibiting the manufacture and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots for five years.

Sources: NBC News (primary)

item.title: US Commerce rule closing remote-access loophole for advanced AI chips rattles Asian data-center buildout
item.description:
A new US export rule restricts foreign parties from remotely using advanced Nvidia compute. Asian data-center operators are scrambling to adjust, and lenders have reportedly paused financing tied to major Chinese cloud providers.

Sources: Semafor (primary), WPNews

item.title: Anthropic says it migrated its Messages API from Python to Rust using Claude agents
item.description:
Anthropic says AI agents compared the Python and Rust implementations against live requests and fixed discrepancies under human review. The company reports about 70% lower CPU use per request and a 20% shorter median time to first token; those figures are its own.

Sources: Anthropic (primary), The Neuron

item.title: Anthropic expands Zurich office to recruit local AI researchers
item.description:
Anthropic is moving into a larger office in Zurich as it seeks to tap the city's pool of AI talent, according to Bloomberg.

Sources: Bloomberg (primary)

item.title: Anthropic lets Claude artifacts be installed as standalone desktop apps in beta
item.description:
Claude artifacts can now be installed as apps on Mac and Windows, with their own windows, notifications and menu bar items. Users choose among three permission levels, including optional full computer access.

Sources: Anthropic (primary), ClaudeDevs on X

item.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after White House pressure
item.description:
Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as chief executive following pressure from the administration. Markets initially rallied, but he still faces congressional and Senate Banking scrutiny over chip export controls and China.

Sources: Tom's Hardware (primary), Semafor, CNBC

item.title: EU proposes 50 billion euro Sovereign Tech Equity Fund for European AI and quantum firms
item.description:
The European Commission put forward a fund targeting 50 billion euros in long-term equity for European AI and quantum companies, alongside a draft Quantum Act favoring EU-controlled suppliers in public procurement. The figure is a target, and the plan still needs negotiation with member states and Parliament.

Sources: DW (primary), European Commission

item.title: Ant Group releases Ling-3.2-air multimodal model with open MIT-licensed weights
item.description:
The model handles text, images and video and is aimed at professional tasks using software tools. Weights can be downloaded and commercially adapted. Ant reports a 61% score on its own office-automation test, versus 15.7% for its earlier Ling-3.0-flash-VL.

Sources: TechNode (primary)

item.title: Amazon says open-source AI agent largely autonomously exploited a zero-day
item.description:
Amazon reported that an open-source AI agent gained unauthorized access by exploiting a previously unknown vulnerability with little human involvement. The case is a notable example of autonomous offensive capability in agents.

Sources: Gizmodo (primary)

item.title: Japan to write goal of becoming a global AI leader behind US and China into security documents
item.description:
Japan plans to add the goal to revised versions of its three main national security documents later this year, with heavy investment in physical AI and automated driving and less reliance on foreign AI. The ruling LDP broadly endorsed the economic security sections at a party meeting.

Sources: Nation Thailand (Jiji Press) (primary)

item.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 models showed intrinsic protein-design ability
item.description:
OpenAI reports that GPT-6 models designed proteins that showed binding to five laboratory targets. The company published the results on its site.

Sources: OpenAI (primary), The Neuron

item.title: Tidal to remove fully AI-generated tracks from its streaming service
item.description:
Tidal says it will delete tracks it identifies as fully AI-generated while still accepting AI-assisted music. The service says fully AI-made tracks made up 43% of uploads over a recent 90-day period.

Sources: The Guardian (primary), TechCrunch

item.title: 42 state attorneys general ask bankruptcy court to block Character.AI's planned sale of user chat histories
item.description:
A bipartisan group of state attorneys general is opposing the Dec. 1 auction of Character.AI's platform, which would include chat data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, about 2.1 million of them minors. They cite child-safety and privacy concerns.

Sources: California Attorney General (primary), TechCrunch

item.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift Amazon's block on Meta's Muse shopping agent
item.description:
Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse AI agent since September. The two companies are now reportedly negotiating terms centered on how search results are presented and on advertising.

Sources: TechCrunch (primary), The Verge

item.title: Epochal launches with $100M to build AI that predicts outcomes, founded by ex-xAI co-founders
item.description:
A new startup founded by three xAI co-founders has emerged with $100 million to train predictive AI models that learn from experience. The company is pitching the approach to developers building such systems.

Sources: SiliconANGLE (primary)

item.title: Walmart and Meta let shoppers buy Black Friday deals inside Meta's Muse assistant
item.description:
Walmart's Agent Gateway is being integrated with Meta's Muse so users can complete purchases in chat. Account-linked spending limits and saved payment methods are supported.

Sources: TechCrunch (primary)

item.title: Staff at Anthropic and OpenAI reportedly warn some advanced models may be too risky to release
item.description:
Axios reports that more than two dozen sources say employees at both labs are worried their most capable unreleased models may not be safe to deploy. The concerns centre on the models' capabilities outpacing current safeguards.

Sources: Axios (primary), SiliconANGLE

item.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok-generated sexualized deepfakes
item.description:
The two states filed suits seeking damages over sexualized images generated by xAI's Grok chatbot. The complaints are allegations that have not been tested in court.

Sources: The Verge (primary), Indian Express

item.title: US adds Alibaba's Singapore unit to entity list in Megaspeed crackdown
item.description:
The Commerce Department blacklisted Alibaba-linked Apex Enterprise Solutions as part of its action against Nvidia-chip reseller Megaspeed. Lawmakers also plan to question Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about China ties.

Sources: The Next Web (primary), The Verge, The Guardian
